data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's diagnostic for mere compliance is structurally uninformative within a single evaluation. It predicts panel accuracy 'collapses on items requiring pruned information,' but if the checklist pruned that information, a genuinely reliable panel should also miss those items. A single evaluation observing low accuracy on such items cannot distinguish the panel merely following the checklist (compliance) from the panel correctly reflecting that the checklist lacks the relevant causal signal. Both explanations yield the same observable accuracy, so the proposed evidence fails to separate genuine reliability bounded by checklist fidelity from mere compliance tracking. The target thus does not identify evidence that distinguishes the two within one evaluation, as required.
